one_month_reasoning: No Synopsys earnings fall in the window (fiscal Q4 FY26 results are due in early December, after the window). What is in the window: (1) how the stock trades after the 30 Sep/1 Oct investor day, when it rose 12.8% to $490.54 on FY27 guidance well above consensus (revenue $11.10-11.20B, non-GAAP EPS $19.04-19.12 vs $17.81 consensus), an AWS IP deal worth over $1B, an OpenAI revenue share and a ~$1B buyback. Base rates favour mild positive drift after a guidance-driven jump: price targets are moving up (BofA $600, KeyBanc $605, Rosenblatt $620, DB $640, HSBC upgrade to $700) and the buyback adds steady demand. Against that, part of the one-day move may give back, since the stock bounced 35% off its 15 Sep low. (2) The FOMC on 27-28 Oct: Polymarket has hold at 74.5% and a 25bp hike at 24.5%. A hike would hit long-duration software multiples. (3) Cadence Q3 results in late October, read across to the sector. (4) Any new AI-EDA disruption headline like Kimi K3 (Jul/Sep 2026), which has moved both EDA stocks 8-10% in a day. Net: median $494 (slightly above spot), log-sd 12% (about annual vol / 3.75, a bit below 45%/3.5 because there is no earnings event), close to symmetric.

fair_value.method: Blend of a forward P/E (FY28 non-GAAP EPS ~$22.5 x 24x = $540, weight 0.6) and an FCF multiple (FY28 FCF/share ~$19.0 x 27x = $514, weight 0.4), giving ~$530 twelve months out.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 non-GAAP EPS $22.5 x 24x forward P/E (the multiple the market will apply in Oct 2027)

inputs_detail.derivation: Comes from ~15% revenue CAGR and a ~50% adjusted operating margin by FY30.
$19.08 x 1.18. I haircut the ~23% target CAGR to ~18% for FY28 because of financing cost on ~$10B of debt (src 1) and execution risk; the 23% pace would give ~$23.5.

Measured on one-year-forward EPS, SNPS was ~40x in Oct 2024 ($513.6 vs FY25 EPS $12.91), ~30x in Oct 2025 ($453.8 vs FY26 guide ~$15.07) and is ~25.7x now on FY27 guide. That is a steady de-rating. Cadence trades at ~43x its 2026 EPS guide ($350.7 / $8.10). With the Fed hiking (Polymarket) and an AI-disruption overhang, I assume the multiple stops falling but does not recover: 24x.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF $3.6B / ~189M diluted shares = $19.0 per share x 27x P/FCF

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 $3.1B grown ~16%, in line with the ~15% revenue CAGR target plus some margin expansion.
193M FY26 guidance less ~$1B+ per year of buybacks at ~$500, net of stock-comp dilution.
Today the stock is ~30x FY27 FCF by market cap ($490.54 x 191M / $3.1B); the Fool cites just over 25x. I take 27x, a mid-point that allows for net debt of ~$6.4B (src 1).

bear.story: Another AI-disruption scare (agent-led open-source design flows), tighter China export curbs (~10% of revenue) or weak Ansys/IP execution, combined with Fed hikes, pushes the multiple to ~17-18x FY28 EPS. The 2025-26 history has three 30%+ drawdowns (Sep-Nov 2025, Jan-Mar 2026, Jun-Jul 2026), so this is not a tail case.

base.story: Synopsys meets or slightly beats FY27 guidance ($19+ EPS, $11.1B+ revenue), FY28 tracks the 15%/23% targets, and the multiple holds at ~24x forward. Buybacks help.

bull.story: AI-agent EDA monetisation (OpenAI, AWS) and hardware verification demand lift growth; the stock re-rates toward 30x FY28 EPS (~$23.5), closing part of the gap to Cadence, which matches HSBC's $700 target.

thesis_break_reason: $370 is about the September 2026 panic low ($362.55), set before management guided FY27 EPS to ~$19. Trading there again would mean under 20x guided EPS and ~22x guided FCF. That would most likely signal that the guidance is not credible (an IP/China miss, AI tools taking share, or an Ansys integration problem) rather than ordinary volatility.

reasoning: Base rates: from monthly closes 2015-2026 (Twelve Data), SNPS's 12-month log return averaged +21% with sd 22% over 10 years, but only +10% with sd 23% over the last 5 years, with 35% of rolling 12-month windows negative. The long-run drift came largely from multiple expansion, and that has reversed: the one-year-forward P/E fell from ~40x (Oct 2024) to ~30x (Oct 2025) to ~25.7x today. Annualised monthly vol is 34% over 5 years and 39% over 2 years, and realised 1-year vol is 45%, so I use a 12-month log-sd of 0.35 above the median and 0.40 below to give a fatter left tail. Since mid-2025 the stock has had three 30%+ drawdowns driven by the IP guidance cut, China curbs and AI-disruption scares. Fundamentals: the 30 Sep investor day reset expectations (FY27 EPS $19.08 vs $17.81 consensus, FCF ~$3.1B, a ~23% EPS CAGR target to FY30, a $1B buyback), and the stock jumped 12.8%. My fair value is $530: 24x FY28 EPS of $22.5 (P/E, weight 0.6) and 27x FY28 FCF per share (weight 0.4). Macro odds from Polymarket: Fed hikes rather than cuts (2 hikes in 2026 at 58.5%), recession by end-2027 at 34.5%, China invading Taiwan by end-2027 at 12.5%. Both are headwinds to a long-duration multiple, which is why I do not assume a re-rating. I set the median at $515 (+5%), below fair value because of the recent pattern of de-rating and the event risk. The ladder gives P(>=491) of 0.55, an expected value of about $525, and an 85% chance of staying above $343. Analyst targets of $600-700 are treated as evidence of upside skew, not as the anchor. Research was limited to about 12 web queries plus Twelve Data price history. Twelve Data statistics and estimates endpoints were not available on this plan.
